sentences.text: Task 3 The Chow family are looking at an exhibition in the Museum called Young Inventors
A guide is showing them around this Exhibition Listen and fill in the missing information in the spaces below.
The first one has been provided as an example.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have one and a half minutes to tidy up your answers.
Hello everyone. My name is Sokari Douglas and I’ll be your guide for this section of the museum.
Today I’ll be showing you the exhibition on young inventors, and I hope you enjoy the tour.
It sounds really interesting.
Do you think it will inspire you to try some inventions of your own, Angela?
Not likely! I’m no good at science.
But I don’t think all the inventions are about science.
Let’s have a look at them.
So Our first exhibit is the shoe battery charger.
This was invented by Juan Domingo from the Philippines, and he was only 14 when he invented it.
The inventor walks 5 kilometers to school every day.
I know this seems a lot, but In the countryside in the Philippines, many school children have to do the same.
Anyway, the inventor thought that this is a lot of wasted energy.
Wow. A 5 kilometer walk to school every day.
That’s pretty far.
Would you like to walk that far to school, Angela?
Not likely! I’m not going to waste all that energy!
Well actually, according to the inventor, on average people take 7 ,000 footsteps a day.
That seems a lot.
So how does the shoe work?
Well, there are different stages to the process and let me show you.
Here is the shoe and inside each shoe are two electrical discs.
First, the person wearing the shoe steps on the electrical discs every time they take a footstep.
Second, each footstep generates pressure on the disc.
And Third, this pressure is then converted to electricity.
So how to use door to electricity?
You need a battery and you attach it to the outside of your shoes.
I’ve got a question.
Yes? How much electricity do the shoes generate?
That’s a good question actually.
At the moment, not so much but this is the first model.
The inventor gave an example: of when he played basketball for an hour and a half, off, he managed to generate 15 minutes of battery power for a mobile phone.
That’s not very much!
That’s right. But there is one other application that the inventor has suggested.
This electricity can be used to power a light, and this doesn’t need so much power.
Any other questions?
What do you think, Angela?
Well, I wouldn’t like to do all the walking, but it certainly is useful.
What do you think, Dad?
I think it’s great.
I worry that is not practical and you won’t be able to produce enough electricity.
Surely traditional batteries are better.
OK, let’s move on to our next invention.
Just over here.
Can everybody see?
This invention is the this seventeen -year -old invented the device for his father, who is deaf
or hard of hearing, I should say.
Jean -Paul invented this to help his father, who couldn’t hear the sound of an alarm clock.
As a result, of this, very often his father was late for work and almost lost his job.
Jean -Paul had the brilliant idea of using the sense of smell instead of sound to wake people up.
Sorry to interrupt, but what smell did Sean Paul find was the most effective to wake people up?
That’s a good question.
And the answer is peppermint.
Peppermint? Yes, peppermint.
So how does the device work then?
Well, first you place some peppermint tablets inside the alarm clock and then you set the alarm.
When the alarm goes off, a fan blows air towards the sleeper.
But does Does it really work?
Oh yes. And you know that most people hate getting up early in the morning?
Well, the inventor reckons that most people wake up in a good mood.
Really? That sounds good to me.
Mm, Sounds too good to be true to me.
And one more thing.
Apparently you also wake up feeling refreshed.
No. I’m not convinced.
I am. I think it sounds fantastic.
What do you think, Angela?
I think I agree with Dad on this one.
